PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 PART 1  PRELIMINARY 

 1  

 Short title and commencement 

 (1)  

 These regulations may be cited as the Prisons Regulations 1968. 

 (2)  

 These regulations shall come into force on 1 August 1960.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 PART 1  PRELIMINARY 

 2  

 Interpretation 

 In these regulations, unless the context otherwise requires— 

 the Act 

 means the Prisons Act 1967 

 Director 

 means the head of the responsible department 

 general order 

 means any general order issued by the Director under regulation 4 hereof 

 officers’ quarters 

 includes any dwellinghouse situated within a prison and occupied by any officer 

 responsible department 

 means the department that, with the authority of the Prime Minister, is for the time being responsible for the administration of the Prisons Act 1967 

 Visiting Justice 

 means a Visiting Justice appointed under section 8 of the Act. 

 Expressions defined in the Act have the meanings so defined.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 PART 1  PRELIMINARY 

 3  

 Application 

 Except as otherwise provided herein, these regulations apply to every prison within the meaning of the Act.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 GENERAL PROVISIONS 

 4  

 General orders 

 The Director may from time to time issue such general orders, not inconsistent with the Act or these regulations, as are necessary or expedient for the administration of the prisons under his or her control and must take such steps as are necessary to ensure that all officers are made aware of the orders.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 GENERAL PROVISIONS 

 5  

 Routine 

 The routine for each prison is as approved by the Director from time to time.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 GENERAL PROVISIONS 

 6  

 Inspection 

 (1)  

 The Visiting Justice must have access to every part of each prison and to all journals, records, and other documents therein relating to the prison or to any inmate thereof; and it is their duty to satisfy themselves on all aspects of the management and control of the prison and its inmates. 

 (2)  

 All orders and instructions given by a Visiting Justice during an inspection of any prison must be entered in the Visiting Justices’ order book and signed by him or her.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 GENERAL PROVISIONS 

 7  

 Women’s quarters 

 (1)  

 In a prison used for the detention of both male and female inmates the quarters set aside for female inmates must be secured by locks different from those used in the rest of the prison. 

 (2)  

 The keys of the quarters set aside for female inmates must, with the exception of one key to the entrance which must be held by the Superintendent, be under the control of female officers, and except in the case of fire, riot or other emergency no male officer or departmental official may enter the premises except on duty and in the company of a female officer.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 GENERAL PROVISIONS 

 8  

 Searching of visitors 

 (1)  

 Every person (including every officer, and every other officer and employee of the Department of responsible department) who enters a prison, and every vehicle brought into a prison, is liable while in the prison to be searched under this regulation. 

 (2)  

 Where the Superintendent has reason to suspect that any person within the prison has any liquor, tobacco, money, or letter, or any article or thing whatsoever, in his or her possession in contravention or intended contravention of section 36 of the Act, the Superintendent may direct that the person be searched. 

 (3)  

 Any other officer who has reason to suspect that any person (not being an officer, and not being any other officer or employee of the Department of responsible department within the prison has any liquor tobacco, money, or letter, or any article or thing whatsoever, in his or her possession in contravention or intended contravention of section 36 of the Act may detain that person detained does not consent to be searched he or she must be brought before the Superintendent, who may direct that the person searched. 

 (4)  

 Reasonable force may used for the purpose of carrying out the search, which must be conducted in as seemly a manner as is consistent with the necessity of discovering any concealed article. 

 (5)  

 No search may be made by or in the presence of any officer of the opposite sex, or (unless the person being searched consents) in the presence of a person temporarily within the prison or of any inmate. 

 (6)  

 Any vehicle brought into a prison may be searched by any officer at any time. 

 (7)  

 A note with all particulars as to the result of any search must be entered in the Superintendent’s journal, and a report must be sent immediately to the Director. 

 (8)  

 This regulation does not apply— 

 (a) 

 to any person visiting the officers’ quarters, if that person does not enter any other part of the prison except on his or her way to and from those quarters; or 

 (b) 

 to any vehicle brought into a prison by any such person and driven or taken only to or from those quarters. 

 [Regulation 8(1): amended, on 1 July 2019, by Schedule 2 of the Ministry of Corrective Services Act 2019 (2019 No 15) .] 

 [Regulation 8(3): amended, on 1 July 2019, by Schedule 2 of the Ministry of Corrective Services Act 2019 (2019 No 15) .]

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 GENERAL PROVISIONS 

 9  

 Visitors to conform to regulations 

 (1)  

 Every person (including every officer, and every other officer and employee of the Department of responsible department) who enters any prison must conform to these regulations and to the other orders and rules governing the prison so far as those regulations, orders, and rules concern him. 

 (2)  

 The Superintendent may refuse to admit to the prison any person who is not willing to conform as aforesaid and may direct the removal from the prison of any person who does not so conform or whose conduct is improper, and may for that purpose use or authorise the use of such force as may be necessary. 

 [Regulation 9(1): amended, on 1 July 2019, by Schedule 2 of the Ministry of Corrective Services Act 2019 (2019 No 15) .]

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 GENERAL PROVISIONS 

 10  

 Visitors to leave in emergency 

 In any case of emergency the Superintendent may ask any person to leave the prison, and may direct the removal of any person who does not leave when asked, and may for that purpose use or authorise the use of such force as may be necessary.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF SUPERINTENDENT 

 11  

 Control of prison 

 (1)  

 The Superintendent of every prison is charged with the control, management, order, and discipline of the prison, with the safe custody of the inmates, and with the care of the journals, registers, books, warrants, and other documents and of all the Government property confided to his or her charge. 

 (2)  

 He or she must produce all journals, records, and documents for inspection by a Visiting Justice when required. 

 (3)  

 He or she must see that his or her officers are fully instructed in their duties and that they perform them with diligence and competence.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF SUPERINTENDENT 

 12  

 Information to be given to inmates 

 (1)  

 The Superintendent must cause a summary approved by the Director of those parts of the Act and of these regulations which relate to inmates to be posted in a conspicuous and accessible part of the prison. 

 (2)  

 He or she must see all inmates as soon as possible after their admission and must satisfy himself or herself that each inmate understands the provisions of the Act and of these regulations governing the treatment of inmates, including those relating to earnings and privileges, to the remission of sentences, to the proper method of making complaints, to food, clothing, bedding, and other necessaries, and to the disciplinary requirements of the prison.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF SUPERINTENDENT 

 13  

 Personal supervision and inspection 

 (1)  

 The Superintendent must exercise close and constant personal supervision of the whole prison, and must see that as far as practicable each inmate is known to him. 

 (2)  

 He or she must at reasonable intervals inspect all parts of the prison and must give special attention to every inmate who is sick or under restraint or undergoing confinement in a cell or upon restricted diet No 1. 

 (3)  

 At least once a week and at uncertain hours he or she must visit the prison at night and satisfy himself or herself that all is in order. 

 (4)  

 He or she must satisfy himself or herself that all gates or outer grilles are locked at the appropriate times, and that the keys are kept at the authorised place or in the possession of the authorised officers. 

 (5)  

 He or she must require reports accounting for all inmates to be made to him or her at the hour of final lock-up, at such times as inmates go and return from work, and at such other times as he or she considers necessary.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF SUPERINTENDENT 

 14  

 Fire precautions 

 The Superintendent must cause to be prepared a set of instructions to be followed in the event of fire and must note these instructions and any change subsequently made to them in his or her order book.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF SUPERINTENDENT 

 15  

 Death of inmate 

 The Superintendent must immediately report the death of any inmate to a Coroner and to one of the Visiting Justices, and must immediately notify the Director and where practicable, the next of kin of the deceased.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF SUPERINTENDENT 

 16  

 Illness of inmate, etc 

 (1)  

 The Superintendent must promptly notify the Director and, where practicable, the next of kin of the inmate, whenever any inmate— 

 (a) 

 becomes seriously ill or suffers serious injury; or 

 (b) 

 is removed to any hospital, or to any institution under the provisions of any enactment. 

 (2)  

 The Superintendent must at once inform an inmate of any intimation he or she receives of the death or serious illness of any near relative of the inmate.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF SUPERINTENDENT 

 17  

 Reports to Director in certain cases 

 The Superintendent must report promptly to the Director whenever any inmate— 

 (a) 

 escapes; or 

 (b) 

 is captured after an escape; or 

 (c) 

 is placed under mechanical restraint; or 

 (d) 

 meets with an accident; or 

 (e) 

 is transferred to another prison; or 

 (f) 

 is transferred to his or her prison from another prison.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF SUPERINTENDENT 

 18  

 Absence of Superintendent 

 (1)  

 The Superintendent must not be away from the vicinity of the prison for more than 24 hours at a time without previously notifying the Director. 

 (2)  

 Before leaving the prison on any occasion he or she must transfer charge to the officer upon whom under these regulations the control of the prison will devolve. 

 (3)  

 If he or she is unable through sickness to perform his or her duties he or she must transfer charge to the officer upon whom under these regulations the control of the prison will devolve, and shall report immediately to the Director. 

 (4)  

 He or she must record any leave or unusual absence in his or her journal.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF SUPERINTENDENT 

 19  

 Books 

 The Superintendent must cause to be kept the books and records shown in the following list and such other books and records as may from time to time be directed by the Director: 

 Admission register: 

 Diary of discharges: 

 Inmates’ property sheets: 

 Visiting Justices’ order book: 

 Journal: 

 Lock-up report book: 

 Medical records as referred to in these regulations: 

 Official visitors’ book: 

 Punishment book: 

 Visitor’s book.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DEPUTY SUPERINTENDENT 

 20  

 Duties and powers 

 (1)  

 Where there is a Deputy Superintendent, then, in the absence of the Superintendent— 

 (a) 

 the Deputy Superintendent has charge of the prison and be responsible in the same manner as the Superintendent: 

 (b) 

 the Deputy Superintendent is not by reason of this subclause entitled to exercise the powers conferred on the Superintendent by section 28 of the Act, but he or she has all the other powers of the Superintendent. 

 (2)  

 The Deputy Superintendent must also exercise, under the direction of the Superintendent, a general supervision of the prison, and has such other powers (except the powers conferred on the Superintendent by section 28 of the Act) and carry out such other duties, as the Superintendent delegates to him.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 OFFICER IN CHARGE OF WOMEN’S QUARTERS 

 21  

 Officer in charge of women’s quarters 

 Where part of any prison is set aside for female inmates that part must, subject to the general control of the Superintendent, be in the charge of a female officer who, unless otherwise authorised, must reside in the prison, and who has the care and superintendence of all female inmates.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 OFFICER IN CHARGE OF WOMEN’S QUARTERS 

 22  

 Personal supervision and inspection 

 (1)  

 The said officer must exercise close and constant personal supervision over every part of the quarters set aside for female inmates, and must see that as far as practicable, every inmate is known to her. 

 (2)  

 She must at reasonable intervals inspect every part of those quarters, and must give special attention to every female inmate who is sick or under restraint or under going confinement in a cell or upon restricted diet No 1. 

 (3)  

 At least once a week at night and at uncertain hours she must go through those quarters and satisfy herself that all is in order.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 OFFICER IN CHARGE OF WOMEN’S QUARTERS 

 23  

 Absence of officer in charge 

 (1)  

 The said officer must not be away from the vicinity of the prison for more than 24 hours at a time without the permission of the Superintendent. 

 (2)  

 Before leaving the prison on any occasion she must transfer charge of the said quarters to such other female officer appointed for the purpose by the Superintendent. 

 (3)  

 If she is unable through sickness to perform her duties she must report immediately to the Superintendent, and must transfer charge to such female officer appointed for the purpose by the Superintendent.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 OFFICER IN CHARGE OF WOMEN’S QUARTERS 

 24  

 Journal 

 (1)  

 The said officer must keep a journal, in which she must record all occurrences of importance within her division. 

 (2)  

 She must submit the journal to the Superintendent and any of the Visiting Justices when required.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 GENERAL RULES AS TO OFFICERS 

 25  

 Devolution of control 

 (1)  

 Unless the Director has directed otherwise, the control of a prison in which male inmates are detained must in the absence of the Superintendent and the Deputy Superintendent (if any) devolve upon the next senior officer available from the following ranks, namely—assistant superintendent, first officer, second officer, third officer, prison officer grade 1 and prison officer grade 2. 

 (2)  

 Unless the Director has directed otherwise, the control of a prison, or any part of a prison, in which female inmates are detained must in the absence of the Superintendent and Deputy Superintendent (if any) or the officer in charge of the quarters set aside for female inmates, as the case may be, devolve upon the next senior matron or assistant matron who is available. 

 (3)  

 Any officer who is in charge of a prison or part of a prison under this regulation must immediately transfer charge to any officer from among the ranks specified in subclause (1) or (2) of this regulation as the case may require who is senior to him or her and who subsequently becomes available and must also transfer charge to the next senior officer from among the ranks so specified if he or she leaves the prison. 

 (4)  

 An officer who has control of a prison under this regulation must for the time being be responsible as if he or she were the Superintendent; and has all the powers of the Superintendent, except that he or she does not by reason of this regulation have the powers conferred on the Superintendent by section 28.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 GENERAL RULES AS TO OFFICERS 

 26  

 Powers in relation to offences 

 The Deputy Superintendent or any other officer having control of the prison may, in the absence of the Superintendent, exercise the powers conferred on the Superintendent under section 28 of the Act subject to the following conditions— 

 (a) 

 that he or she has the prior authority of the Director: 

 (b) 

 that he or she complies with any restriction imposed by the Director on the extent of his or her exercise of those powers.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 GENERAL RULES AS TO OFFICERS 

 27  

 Officers in charge 

 Unless the Superintendent has directed otherwise, the control of a particular post or body of officers devolves, in the absence of the officer in charge of that post or body of officers, upon the senior officer present.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 GENERAL RULES AS TO OFFICERS 

 28  

 Duties of officers 

 Every officer must perform such duties as the Superintendent from time to time directs, and must carry out any extra or special duty when directed.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 GENERAL RULES AS TO OFFICERS 

 29  

 Emergencies 

 In any case of emergency every officer is expected to act promptly, to use his or her own judgment, and to exercise initiative.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 GENERAL RULES AS TO OFFICERS 

 30  

 Obedience to orders 

 Every officer must obey without question any lawful order given by his or her senior officer; but he or she may afterwards appeal to the Superintendent or, if the order was given by the Superintendent, to the Director.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 GENERAL RULES AS TO OFFICERS 

 31  

 Association with discharged inmates 

 No officer may associate with any discharged inmate, or with the wife, husband, parents, children, brothers, or sisters of an inmate or a discharged inmate, except with the consent of the Superintendent.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 GENERAL RULES AS TO OFFICERS 

 32  

 Non-disclosure of information 

 Except in the performance of his or her official duties or unless he or she has the permission of the Superintendent, no officer may communicate beyond the prison any occurrence within any prison, or in any way disclose the identity of any inmate or discharged inmate or the fact that any person is or has been an inmate of any prison.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 GENERAL RULES AS TO OFFICERS 

 33  

 Trading with inmates 

 (1)  

 No officer may at any time receive any money, gratuity, reward, or benefit of any kind from or on behalf of any inmate, nor may he or she trade with or enter into any agreement with any inmate. 

 (2)  

 Unless authorised in writing by the Superintendent or the Director, no officer may purchase any article from or belonging to any inmate, or any article made in the prison, or have any work done for him or her by any inmate.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 GENERAL RULES AS TO OFFICERS 

 34  

 Health of inmates 

 Any officer who notices that any inmate does not appear to be in good health, although he or she may not complain, or that his or her state of mind appears to be deserving of notice or care, must inform the Superintendent in order that the opinion and instructions of the medical officer may be obtained.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 GENERAL RULES AS TO OFFICERS 

 35  

 Personal visitors 

 (1)  

 Except by permission of the Superintendent, no officer is permitted to receive or take personal visitors within any part of the prison other than the officers’ quarters. 

 (2)  

 Officers’ personal visitors are subject to regulations hereof. 

 (3)  

 The Superintendent may at any time refuse to allow any person access to the quarters in which single officers are living. 

 (4)  

 No private person (including any member of an officer’s family) may have access to an officer on duty except by permission of the Superintendent.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 GENERAL RULES AS TO OFFICERS 

 36  

 Liquor, tobacco, etc 

 The provisions of section 36(1) of the Act do not apply to any liquor, tobacco, money; or letter, or any article or thing whatsoever, that an officer brings or causes to be brought into the officers’ quarters.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 GENERAL RULES AS TO OFFICERS 

 37  

 Liquor in prisons 

 (1)  

 Except under such restrictions as to time and place as may be specified by the Superintendent and approved by the Director, no officer may have or use intoxicating liquor within any part of the prison other than the officers’ quarters. 

 (2)  

 The Superintendent may at any time restrict the use of intoxicating liquor in any officers’ quarters that are in close proximity to inmates’ quarters.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 GENERAL RULES AS TO OFFICERS 

 38  

 Representations on matters affecting officers’ interests 

 (1)  

 Officers are entitled to make representations, either to the Superintendent or through the Superintendent to the Director, on any matter that affects their interests. 

 (2)  

 Any officer wishing to bring any matter before the Director may make a written statement to the Superintendent, who must forthwith forward the statement with his or her comments to the Director. 

 (3)  

 Officers may hold meetings to discuss any matter that affects their interests, but no meeting may be held for the purpose of formulating a charge against any other officer or for the purpose of instigating or inciting disobedience to orders or for any other purpose prejudicial to discipline.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 PERSONS VIEWING PRISONS 

 39  

 Permission to view prisons 

 (1)  

 The Superintendent may permit reputable persons or members of an organisation to view the prison. 

 (2)  

 The names of persons or of organisations permitted to view the prison must be entered in the Superintendent’s journal.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 PERSONS VIEWING PRISONS 

 40  

 Communication with inmates, and information 

 (1)  

 No person viewing the prison may in any way communicate with any inmate except with the permission of the Superintendent. 

 (2)  

 No inmate is to be pointed out to any such person, and no information whatever regarding any inmate is to be given to any such person.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 PERSONS VIEWING PRISONS 

 41  

 Non-disclosure of information 

 (1)  

 No person who has been permitted to view a prison may disclose to any other person the identity or place of detention of any inmate or any information concerning any person who was an inmate at the time of the visit. 

 (2)  

 Any person who commits a breach of this regulation is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $10.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 PART 3  TREATMENT OF INMATES 

 42  

 Application 

 The provisions of this Part of these regulations apply to every inmate, except so far as they are inconsistent with the special provisions of Part 5 hereof.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 ADMISSION AND DISCHARGE 

 43  

 Times for admission and discharge 

 No inmate may be received or discharged before 7 am or after 8 pm, except in special circumstances.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 ADMISSION AND DISCHARGE 

 44  

 Register 

 (1)  

 In every prison there must be an admission register, in which there must be entered in respect of each inmate the following particulars: 

 (a) 

 information concerning his or her identity: 

 (b) 

 the authority for his or her committal and the offence in respect of which he or she has been committed: 

 (c) 

 the day of his or her admission and discharge: 

 (d) 

 such other particulars as may be directed by the Director by general order. 

 (2)  

 Except where the prison is used as a lock-up as provided in subclause (3) or where otherwise allowed by law, no inmate may be received in a prison without a valid committal order of which the details must be entered in the register. 

 (3)  

 With the consent of the Director, the Police may use any prison as a lock-up provided all reasonable steps are taken by the Police to bring any person detained in such lock-up before a Judge or a Commissioner of the High Court as soon as practicable.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 ADMISSION AND DISCHARGE 

 45  

 Search of inmate on admission 

 (1)  

 Every inmate upon admission must be completely searched, and all property (other than toilet requisites, other personal articles, and books, approved by the Superintendent) must be taken from him or her. 

 (2)  

 The provisions of regulation 67 hereof apply to every search under this regulation. 

 (3)  

 Any ring worn by an inmate may be cut off if it cannot be otherwise removed.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 ADMISSION AND DISCHARGE 

 46  

 Property of inmate on admission 

 All property taken from any inmate on his or her admission, and any of his or her property (other than toilet requisites, other personal articles, and books, approved by the Superintendent) that is brought into the prison after his or her admission, must be placed in the charge of the Superintendent: 
 Provided that the Superintendent may refuse to receive any article into his or her charge, and may in any such case, on behalf of the inmate, make arrangements for the storage of the article at the inmate’s expense.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 ADMISSION AND DISCHARGE 

 47  

 Inmate’s property sheet 

 An inventory specifying in detail every article placed in the charge of the Superintendent and every article retained by the inmate with the Superintendent’s approval must be entered on an inmate’s property sheet, which must be signed by the inmate.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 ADMISSION AND DISCHARGE 

 48  

 Bathing of inmate on admission 

 Every inmate, unless exempted by the Superintendent or the medical officer, must be thoroughly washed and cleansed before being placed among other inmates.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 ADMISSION AND DISCHARGE 

 49  

 Disposal of liquor and perishable or dangerous goods 

 Any intoxicating liquor, or any perishable inflammable, or dangerous substance, belonging to an inmate may be poured away or destroyed in the presence of the inmate, and if that is done a note must be made on his or her inmate’s property sheet.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 ADMISSION AND DISCHARGE 

 50  

 Clothing 

 (1)  

 Underclothing, and if necessary any article of outer clothing, must be washed or cleaned before being stored. 

 (2)  

 If any article of clothing is filthy or infected it may be destroyed in the presence of the inmate on the direction of the medical officer, and a note must be made on the inmate’s property sheet.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 ADMISSION AND DISCHARGE 

 51  

 Property of inmate on release 

 (1)  

 Any inmate may see and inspect his or her property at any one time within 1 month before the date on which he or she is to be released, and may be allowed to check it with the original inventory or a certified copy. 

 (2)  

 The inmate’s property must be returned to him or her on his or her release, and he or she must sign the inmate’s property sheet as a receipt.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 ADMISSION AND DISCHARGE 

 52  

 Discharged inmate may remain in interests of health 

 Any person who is entitled to be released from a prison must be formally discharged, but may be permitted by the Superintendent to remain in the prison so long as the medical officer certifies in writing that it is in the interests of that person’s health that he or she should remain.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 ADMISSION AND DISCHARGE 

 53  

 Female inmate with child 

 Any female inmate who gives birth to a child or who on admission has a child less than 6 months old, may keep the child with her until proper provision is made for its care.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 TRANSFER AND REMOVAL 

 54  

 Removal of property on transfer of inmate 

 When any inmate is transferred from one prison to another, his or her property, if any, and his or her inmate’s property sheet must be forwarded to the Superintendent of the prison to which he or she is transferred.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 TRANSFER AND REMOVAL 

 55  

 Privacy 

 While any inmate is being transferred to or removed from a prison he or she must be exposed to public view as little as possible.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 TRANSFER AND REMOVAL 

 56  

 Mechanical restraint 

 (1)  

 In the case of any inmate being transferred or removed from, or being returned to, a prison under escort, the Superintendent of the prison from which the escort is dispatched may direct that mechanical restraint be used. 

 (2)  

 In any case where the Superintendent has not directed that mechanical restraint be used, the officer in charge of the escort may use mechanical restraint if he or she considers that course advisable in the circumstances.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 TRANSFER AND REMOVAL 

 57  

 Complete search of inmate 

 (1)  

 Any inmate who is being transferred from one prison to another must be completely searched immediately before, and immediately after, each days travelling and, wherever possible, must be searched on every occasion on which a stop is made for a meal. 

 (2)  

 The provisions of regulation 67 hereof apply to every search under this regulation. 

 (3)  

 Every search required by this regulation must be made in the presence of the officer in charge of the escort. 

 (4)  

 Where any such search is made at any prison, it is the joint responsibility of the Superintendent of the prison and of the officer in charge of the escort to see that this regulation is complied with. 

 (5)  

 Where any such search is made elsewhere it is the responsibility of the officer in charge of the escort to see that this regulation is complied with.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 TRANSFER AND REMOVAL 

 58  

 Communication with public, liquor 

 (1)  

 As far as practicable an officer on escort duty must not permit any inmate to communicate with any member other public. 

 (2)  

 An officer on escort duty must not drink intoxicating liquor or permit any inmate to do so.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 GENERAL PROVISIONS AS TO DISCIPLINE AND CONTROL 

 59  

 Maintenance of discipline and responsibility 

 (1)  

 Discipline and order must be maintained with firmness, and fairness; and, in the control of inmates, officers must seek to influence them through example and leadership and to enlist their willing cooperation. 

 (2)  

 At all times in the treatment of inmates officers must have regard to the aim of rehabilitation and the encouragement of self-respect and a sense of personal responsibility.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 GENERAL PROVISIONS AS TO DISCIPLINE AND CONTROL 

 60  

 Duty of officers as to custody 

 Every officer must exercise the utmost care and vigilance in the custody and surveillance of the inmates under his or her charge, and must not part with the custody of an inmate otherwise than in accordance with orders or by handing him or her over to another officer.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 GENERAL PROVISIONS AS TO DISCIPLINE AND CONTROL 

 61  

 Use of force 

 (1)  

 No officer may use force in dealing with any inmate except in self-defence or in the defence of another person, or in the case of escape or attempted escape or active or passive physical resistance to a lawful order. 

 (2)  

 Any officer who uses force pursuant to this regulation must use no more than if necessary in the circumstances. The officer must report the incident to the Superintendent as soon as possible. 

 (3)  

 No officer may deliberately act or speak in a manner likely to provoke an inmate.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 GENERAL PROVISIONS AS TO DISCIPLINE AND CONTROL 

 62  

 Obedience by inmates 

 (1)  

 Every inmate must promptly obey every lawful order that is given to him or her. 

 (2)  

 Any inmate who considers himself or herself aggrieved by an order must nevertheless obey but may on the first convenient occasion complain to the Superintendent or a Visiting Justice.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 GENERAL PROVISIONS AS TO DISCIPLINE AND CONTROL 

 63  

 Cleanliness of cell, etc 

 Every inmate must keep himself, his or her sleeping quarters, and the furniture therein, in the highest state of cleanliness and tidiness.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 GENERAL PROVISIONS AS TO DISCIPLINE AND CONTROL 

 64  

 Inmate not to be employed in disciplinary capacity 

 No inmate may be employed in a disciplinary capacity.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 SEARCHING 

 65  

 Searching of inmates 

 (1)  

 Any inmate may be searched at any time. 

 (2)  

 Every inmate must be searched after returning from work. 

 (3)  

 Every inmate must be searched before being brought into the presence of the Director or a Visiting Justice. 

 (4)  

 Every inmate must be completely searched before being locked in a cell under report or punishment.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 SEARCHING 

 66  

 Conduct of search 

 (1)  

 The searching of an inmate must be conducted in as seemly a manner as is consistent with the necessity of discovering any concealed article. 

 (2)  

 No inmate may be searched by or in the presence of any officer of the opposite sex. 

 (3)  

 Two officers must always be present whenever any inmate is being completely searched. 

 (4)  

 No other inmate may be present while any inmate is being completely searched.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 SEARCHING 

 67  

 Exemptions 

 (1)  

 The Director may from time to time direct that all or any of the provisions of regulation 65(2) and (3) hereof, do not apply to any particular prison. 

 (2)  

 The Director, may from time to the authorise the Superintendent of any prison to direct that for a specified period, not exceeding the period for which authority is granted, all or any of the said provisions do not apply to that prison. 

 (3)  

 Any direction or authority given under this regulation may at any time be varied or revoked.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 COMPLAINTS BY INMATES 

 68  

 Requests to see Superintendent 

 Within a week of the application being made, the Superintendent must hear the application of every inmate who has made a request to see him.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 COMPLAINTS BY INMATES 

 69  

 Interviews with Visiting Justices 

 (1)  

 Every inmate has the right to interview a Visiting Justice visiting the prison. 

 (2)  

 Any inmate who wishes to exercise the right given by this regulation, must first apply to the Superintendent to have his or her name placed on a list kept for the purpose.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 HEARING OF CHARGES 

 70  

 Inmate reported for offence 

 When any inmate has been reported for an offence the charge against him or her must be heard as soon as possible.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 HEARING OF CHARGES 

 71  

 Procedure on charge 

 (1)  

 Whenever any inmate is charged with an offence against discipline under section 26 of the Act, he or she must be notified of the charge a sufficient time before the hearing to enable him or her to prepare his or her defence. 

 (2)  

 Where the Visiting Justice or Superintendent hearing the charge is satisfied that the inmate has not had a proper opportunity to prepare his or her defence the hearing or the charge must be adjourned.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 HEARING OF CHARGES 

 72  

 Prosecutor 

 At the hearing of any charge against an inmate, any officer, not being the Superintendent or any other officer who is for the time being entitled under regulation 26 to exercise the powers conferred on the Superintendent under section 28 of the Act may conduct the proceedings on behalf of the person making the charge.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 HEARING OF CHARGES 

 73  

 Procedure at hearing 

 (1)  

 At the commencement of the hearing the charge must be read to the inmate, who must then be asked how he or she pleads. 

 (2)  

 If the inmate pleads guilty he or she must be given an opportunity to make an explanation before any penalty is imposed. 

 (3)  

 If the inmate pleads not guilty the case against him or her must be presented, and he or she must then be given an opportunity to present his or her own case and to call witnesses on his or her behalf. Any witnesses may be cross examined. 

 (4)  

 If after hearing all the evidence the Visiting Justice or the Superintendent, as the case may be, is satisfied that the case against the inmate is proved he or she shall so inform the inmate, and before imposing any penalty he or she must give the inmate an opportunity to make an explanation.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 PUNISHMENTS 

 74  

 Restricted diets 

 (1)  

 Every inmate sentenced to restricted diet under section 27 or 28 of the Act shall be sentenced to be placed on either No 1 diet, as prescribed, by subclause (2), or No 2 diet, as prescribed in subclause (3) of this regulation. 

 (2)  

 No 1 diet shall each day consist of 8 oz of bread, 2lbs of taro, 1½ pints of milk, and 1 oz of dripping: 
 Provided that where under the said section 27 the period for which No 1 diet is ordered exceeds 3 days the inmate shall be given full rations on every fourth day. 

 (3)  

 No 2 diet shall each day consist of: 

 Food 
 Quantity 

 Bread 
 1 lb 

 Taro 
 12 oz 

 Salt 
 ½ oz 

 Sugar 
 2 oz 

 Milk 
 1 pint 

 Cheese 
 2 oz 

 Dripping 
 2 oz

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 PUNISHMENTS 

 75  

 Commencement of sentence of restricted diet 

 No sentence of restricted diet shall commence until after the medical officer has certified in writing that the inmate is in a fit condition of health to sustain it.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 PUNISHMENTS 

 76  

 Treatment of inmate on No 1 diet 

 (1)  

 Every inmate on No 1 diet shall be confined in a punishment cell. He or she shall not be required to work. 

 (2)  

 He or she shall be given 1 hour’s exercise a day, unless the medical officer otherwise directs. 

 (3)  

 He or she shall have all privileges withdrawn: 
 Provided that the Director may at any time by general order direct that any specified privilege shall not be withdrawn under this regulation. 

 (4)  

 Except with the approval of the Superintendent in a case of emergency, he or she shall not be permitted to receive any visitors under regulation 106, or to write or receive any letters: 
 Provided that he or she shall be permitted to write one letter immediately after the sentence has been passed. 

 (5)  

 He or she shall be visited at least once day by the Superintendent, and at intervals of not more than 3 hours during the day by an officer appointed for that purpose.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 PUNISHMENTS 

 77  

 Restriction on further sentence 

 No inmate who has been on No 1 diet shall be sentenced to that diet for a fresh offence until an interval has elapsed equal to the period already spent by the inmate on No 1 diet.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 PUNISHMENTS 

 78  

 Treatment of inmate on No 2 diet 

 (1)  

 Every inmate on No 2 diet shall have all privileges withdrawn: 
 Provided that the Director may at any time by general order direct that any specified privilege shall not be withdrawn under this regulation. 

 (2)  

 Except with the approval of the Superintendent in a case of emergency, he or she shall not be permitted to receive any visitors under regulation 106, or to write or receive any letters: 
 Provided that he or she shall be permitted to write one letter immediately after the sentence has been passed.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 PUNISHMENTS 

 79  

 Sentence of confinement in cell 

 (1)  

 Every inmate sentenced to confinement in a cell must be kept in cell by himself or herself for the period of the confinement. 

 (2)  

 He or she must not work, unless work which can be done in the cell is available. 

 (3)  

 He or she must be given one hour’s exercise a day, unless the medical officer otherwise directs. 

 (4)  

 He or she is not permitted to receive any visitors under regulation 106. 

 (5)  

 He or she must be visited at least once a day by the Superintendent, and at intervals of not more than 3 hours during the day by an officer appointed for that purpose.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 PENAL GRADE 

 80  

 Transfer of inmate to penal grade 

 The Director or a Visiting Justice may direct the transfer to the penal grade of any inmate who has on 3 or more occasions been found guilty, whether by the Superintendent or a Visiting Justice or by a court, of conduct or acts which are offences against discipline under section 26(1) of the Act or who has been found guilty, whether by a Visiting Justice or by a court, of any conduct or act which is an offence against discipline under section 26(2).

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 PENAL GRADE 

 81  

 Treatment of inmate in penal grade 

 (1)  

 Any inmate who has been transferred to the penal grade may be placed in a separate part of the prison. 

 (2)  

 The inmate is not allowed to associate with other inmates except when at work or at worship; and he or she may be excluded from association at work also if the Superintendent so directs. 

 (3)  

 The value of every earnings mark allotted to him or her is the minimum rate approved from time to time under section 17(3) of the Act. 

 (4)  

 He or she is not allowed to receive any gift parcels. 

 (5)  

 He or she is not allowed to receive visitors under regulation 106 hereof more often than once in any fortnight. 

 (6)  

 He or she is not allowed to make any, purchase at the canteen, except one ounce of tobacco together with 1 box of matches and 1 packet of cigarette papers a week and toilet necessities. 

 (7)  

 He or she must wear such distinctive marks on his or her clothes, or such distinctive clothing, as is prescribed by the Director, by general order.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 PENAL GRADE 

 82  

 Release from penal grade 

 Any inmate transferred to the penal grade may at any time be released from that grade by direction of the Director or a Visiting Justice, and must be so released at the end of 3 months if no direction has been given.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 EARNINGS 

 83  

 Amount of earnings 

 The amount of earnings to be credited to any inmate must be determined by the Superintendent from time to time.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 EARNINGS 

 84  

 Marks allotted to inmates 

 The amount of earnings for the time being standing to the credit of each inmate must be notified to him or her once a month on request.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 EARNINGS 

 85  

 Spending in canteen 

 Every inmate may be permitted to spend in the canteen such part of his or her earnings as the Director from time to time determines.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 EARNINGS 

 86  

 Earnings account 

 The part of his or her earnings that an inmate is not allowed to spend in the canteen must be retained in an earnings account.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 EARNINGS 

 87  

 Deductions 

 With the approval of the Director or the Superintendent there may be deducted from the earnings previously credited, or subsequently to be credited, to any inmate the value or part of the value of any article of departmental property that in the opinion of the Superintendent was wilfully damaged or destroyed, or lost through the carelessness or improper conduct of the inmate.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 EARNINGS 

 88  

 Expenditure by inmate 

 The Director or the Superintendent may approve any expenditure by an inmate from the earnings previously credited or subsequently to be credited to him.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 EARNINGS 

 89  

 Payments to dependants 

 The Director or the Superintendent may from time to time in special cases direct that the amount of earnings credited to any inmate or any portion of the earnings, be paid to the inmate’s dependants.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 EARNINGS 

 90  

 Payment of accumulated earnings 

 (1)  

 On the release of any inmate on probation he or she must be paid such portion of his or her accumulated earnings as the Superintendent approves. Any balance must be paid through the probation officer supervising him or her at such times during the period of probation and in such amounts as the probation officer thinks fit. 

 (2)  

 On the release of any other inmate he or she must be paid the full amount of his or her accumulated earnings.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 RELIGION 

 91  

 Religious observance 

 (1)  

 The Director must, encourage and facilitate religious observance in each prison, and must make all proper provision for the spiritual welfare of inmates. 

 (2)  

 The Director may enter into any arrangement with any organisation or group of churches for the appointment to any prison of a chaplain to represent all denominations of which the organisation or group is composed.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 RELIGION 

 92  

 Religious services 

 (1)  

 Where a chaplain has been appointed to a prison under section 5(2) of the Act he or she must conduct services in that prison for the denomination to which he or she belongs and for any other denomination which he or she represents, and must minister to the spiritual needs of inmates belonging to those denominations. 

 (2)  

 Any Priest of the Roman Catholic Church may at convenient times hold services in any prison in which members of that church are inmates. 

 (3)  

 With the approval of the Director services may be held at convenient times in each prison by any minister of religion of any other denomination to which inmates belong. 

 (4)  

 Any inmate may be required to attend services of the denomination to which he or she belongs, or those conducted by any chaplain who represents the denomination to which the inmate belongs.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 RELIGION 

 93  

 Visits by ministers of religion 

 Any minister of religion may at convenient times visit any inmate for whom he or she has a pastoral responsibility; 
 Provided that no inmate is required to receive a visit from any minister of religion if he or she objects to the visit.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 RELIGION 

 94  

 Denomination of inmate 

 The denomination of any inmate shall be determined by his or her voluntary statement on his or her admission inmate may change his or her denomination from time to time by notifying the Superintendent, but no inmate under the age of 21 years may change his or her denomination without prior reference to his or her parents or guardian or, if they are dead or cannot be communicated with readily, to the Director.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 RELIGION 

 95  

 Exemptions from work 

 (1)  

 Except in an emergency, no inmate is required to work at any tasks, other than those necessary for the service of the prison, on Sunday or Saturday in the case or an adherent of the Seventh Day Adventist faith, Christmas Day, Good Friday, or Anzac Day. 

 (2)  

 The Superintendent may in his or her discretion exempt any inmate from working on any of his or her recognised days of religious observance.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 EDUCATION 

 96  

 Assistance to inmates 

 Every inmate who wishes to improve his or her education must be given such assistance as is reasonable and practicable in the circumstances.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 EDUCATION 

 97  

 Facilities 

 In each prison there must be provided such facilities for primary and post-primary education as the Director may approve from time to time.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 EDUCATION 

 98  

 Training 

 Training courses must be provided in such trades, occupations, and industries as the Director may approve.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 EDUCATION 

 99  

 Higher education 

 Any inmate may, with the approval of the Director, undertake a course in higher education or a specialist course.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 EDUCATION 

 100  

 Fees for higher education 

 Any fees and other expenses of any such course in higher education or specialist course must be paid by the inmate, except in any special case approved by the Director. Despite any such approval given by the Director, the Director may require any fees or other expenses of any such course in higher that education or specialist course be charged to the inmate if his or her conduct at classes or lectures or his or her diligence is not satisfactory.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 EDUCATION 

 101  

 Attendance 

 Attendance at classes in primary education may be made compulsory for any inmate if the Superintendent is of the opinion that his or her standard of education is too low and that he or she would benefit from further education. Attendance at any other course, class, or lecture may be made compulsory for any inmate if the Superintendent considers such course, class, or lecture would be beneficial to the inmate.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 EDUCATION 

 102  

 Hours for instruction 

 Except with the approval of the Director, educational activities must not be followed in hours prescribed for work.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 EDUCATION 

 103  

 Duties of teachers 

 Every teacher appointed to a teaching position in a prison must undertake such duties, consistent with his or her appointment, as the Director determines.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 CORRESPONDENCE 

 104  

 Letters 

 (1)  

 Subject to the provisions of regulations 76 and 78 hereof, every inmate may in each week write 3 letters and receive 3 letters. 

 (2)  

 The Superintendent may allow any inmate whose conduct is satisfactory to write or receive additional letters. 

 (3)  

 Except with the written authority of the Director or a Visiting Justice, no inmate is permitted to write to any other inmate. 

 (4)  

 The Director or a Visiting Justice or the Superintendent may prohibit any inmate from writing to or receiving letters from any particular person. 

 (5)  

 The Superintendent may refuse to permit any inmate to send or to receive any letter not written in English or Maori, and may cause to be translated any letter not written in English or Maori.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 CORRESPONDENCE 

 104A  

 Communication by inmate to Minister 

 (1)  

 Despite the provisions of regulations 76, 78, 104, and 105 any inmate has the right at any time to communicate in writing to the Minister. 

 (2)  

 Every communication made by an inmate under subclause (1) must not be examined read or opened by the Superintendent or any other person other than the Minister. 

 (3)  

 Every communication made by an inmate under subclause (1) must be recorded by the Superintendent or any person acting on his or her behalf in a book or register kept for that purpose and must be conveyed or delivered as speedily as possible to the Minister. 

 (4)  

 Every communication made by an inmate under subclause (1) may be replied to or dealt with by the Minister in such manner as he or she thinks fit. 

 [Regulation 104A: inserted, on 29 November 1978, by regulation 2 of the Prisons Regulations 1968 Amendment No 1 1978 (SN 1978/7) .]

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 CORRESPONDENCE 

 105  

 Examination and disposal of letters and parcels 

 (1)  

 No inmate may send or receive any letter, parcel, or article except through the Superintendent. 

 (2)  

 Every letter or parcel sent by or intended for any inmate must be opened, and its contents examined, by the Superintendent or by a responsible officer nominated by him or her for the purpose: 
 Provided that the Director may from time to time direct that the provisions of this subclause do not apply to any particular prison either wholly or to such extent as the Superintendent thinks fit or to such extent as is specified by the Director. 

 (3)  

 The Superintendent must retain any article which is of a type not approved by the Director by general order, or any letter, parcel, or article that, in the Superintendent’s opinion— 

 (a) 

 may affect the discipline or security of the prison; or 

 (b) 

 has been brought into the prison in contravention of the Act or of any regulation; or 

 (c) 

 consists of or contains any objectionable or illegal matter, or refers in any way to any illegal transaction; or 

 (d) 

 may adversely affect any other person. 

 (4)  

 Any letter intended for an inmate and retained under this regulation must be returned to the sender, unless it consists of or contains any illegal matter, or refers in any way to any illegal transaction. 

 (5)  

 Any parcel or article intended for an inmate and retained under this regulation, unless it consists of or contains illegal matter, must either be returned to the sender or kept with the inmate’s property; 
 Provided that any intoxicating liquor or any perishable, inflammable or dangerous substance must be poured away or destroyed in the presence of the inmate instead of being returned or kept as aforesaid. 

 (6)  

 Subject to the provisions of these regulations, any inmate may be permitted to receive and retain in his or her cell any article intended for him or her which is of a type approved by the Director by general order. 

 [Regulation 105(6): amended, on 11 November 1981, by regulation 3(1) of the Prisons Regulations 1968 Amendment No 1 1981 (SN 1981/8) .]

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 VISITS 

 106  

 Visitors 

 (1)  

 Subject to the provisions of regulations 76, 78, 79, and 107, every inmate whose work and conduct are satisfactory, not being an inmate awaiting trial or sentence, is permitted to receive visitors during a period of not less than 30 minutes each Saturday, Sundays, or on such part of any other day as the Director may approve in respect of any particular prison. 

 (2)  

 Except in special circumstances not more than 3 visitors are allowed to visit an inmate at anyone time. 

 (3)  

 Subject to the provisions of regulations 76, 78, 79, and 107, if the prison is isolated, or if a visitor has travelled from a distance, or if other special circumstances exist, the Superintendent may allow a visit on a day other than a Saturday. 

 (4)  

 Every person wishing to visit an inmate must give his or her name and address to the appropriate officer.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 VISITS 

 107  

 Power to refuse permission 

 (1)  

 The Superintendent must refuse permission to any person to visit an inmate if he or she thinks that the visit may affect the security or discipline of the prison, and may refuse permission if he or she thinks that the character or conduct of the person applying for admission is undesirable or for any other sufficient reason. 

 (2)  

 No person known to the Superintendent to be a former inmate shall be permitted to visit an inmate except where approved by the Director.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 VISITS 

 108  

 Supervision 

 (1)  

 A general supervision of visits must be exercised, but at the discretion of the Superintendent they may be held in reasonable privacy. 

 (2)  

 If the officer supervising any visit considers that the visit is taking a course that may affect the security or discipline of the prison, or that the conduct of either the inmate or a visitor is undesirable, he or she may bring the visit to a close and may report the visitor, before he or she leaves the prison, to the Superintendent.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 VISITS 

 109  

 Legal advisers 

 The legal adviser of any inmate may, with the prior permission of the Superintendent, at any time interview the inmate with reference to any legal business not pertaining to the discipline of the prison, and any such visit is additional to those allowed under the foregoing regulations.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 VISITS 

 110  

 Police 

 Any member of the Police may visit any inmate if the Superintendent or another officer is present at the beginning of the interview. If the inmate expresses unwillingness to see the Police, the visit may be terminated by the said Superintendent or officer.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 VISITS 

 111  

 Inmates committed in default of payment 

 A person committed to a prison in default of the payment of a sum of money which in pursuance of any conviction or order his or her required to pay must be allowed to have an interview with his or her friends on a week day at any reasonable hour, or to communicate by letter with them, for the purpose of providing for a payment which would procure his or her release.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 SOCIAL RELATIONS AND AFTER CARE 

 112  

 Rehabilitation 

 (1)  

 Throughout the sentence of every inmate, consideration must be given to his or her rehabilitation. 

 (2)  

 So far as practicable and in the opinion of the Superintendent desirable, an inmate must be encouraged and assisted to maintain or establish such relations with persons or organisations outside the prison as may promote his or her rehabilitation and the best interests of his or her family. 

 (3)  

 Where under this regulation any person is permitted to visit any inmate, the visit is additional to visits allowed under regulation 106.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 SOCIAL RELATIONS AND AFTER CARE 

 113  

 Identity of inmates not to be disclosed 

 No person permitted under regulation 112 to enter a prison may disclose to any other person the identity or place of detention of any inmate or any information concerning any person who was an inmate at the time of the visit, except with the consent of the inmate.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 MEDICAL AND DENTAL FACILITIES 

 114  

 Medical and dental facilities 

 (1)  

 Unless the Director directs in respect of any prison, there must be provided and maintained in each prison a room suitably equipped for the carrying out of medical and dental examinations and treatment. 

 (2)  

 It is the responsibility of the medical officer to advise the Superintendent so that the medical equipment is properly maintained and the necessary medical supplies are available. 

 (3)  

 It is the responsibility of the dental officer to advise the Superintendent so that the dental equipment is properly maintained and the necessary dental supplies are available. 

 (4)  

 It is their joint responsibility to advise the Superintendent so that the provisions of the Narcotics Act 1966 are observed.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF MEDICAL OFFICER 

 115  

 Visits 

 The medical officer must visit the prison at such periods as may be specified by the Director, and at other times on the request of the Superintendent.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF MEDICAL OFFICER 

 116  

 Supervision 

 (1)  

 The medical officer must do everything necessary to maintain the good health of inmates, and must recommend to the Superintendent any special remedial treatment or the modification of any punishment or treatment likely to affect the well-being of any inmate. 

 (2)  

 The medical officer must pay special attention to the health of anyone confined in a punishment cell.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF MEDICAL OFFICER 

 117  

 Medical examinations 

 (1)  

 The medical officer must examine every inmate as soon after admission as possible, and must enter the required particulars on a reception medical examination record card. 

 (2)  

 The medical officer enter on the inmate’s clinical record card details of any subsequent examinations.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF MEDICAL OFFICER 

 118  

 Prescription book 

 The medical officer must keep a prescription book in which he or she must enter, in duplicate, all prescriptions ordered for inmates.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF MEDICAL OFFICER 

 119  

 X-ray examinations 

 Wherever desirable in the case of any inmate whose sentence is longer than one month, and in any other case where the medical officer considers it necessary, the medical officer must ensure that a chest x-ray is carried out as soon as possible after the inmate’s admission and, where applicable, thereafter at 6 monthly intervals.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF MEDICAL OFFICER 

 120  

 Transfers to hospital 

 Where the medical officer considers that any inmate should be transferred to a public hospital, he or she must recommend such transfer and must give the particulars of the case to the Superintendent.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF MEDICAL OFFICER 

 121  

 Additional medical assistance 

 In an emergency the medical officer may, without the prior consent of the Director, but with the knowledge of the Superintendent, call in additional medical assistance.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF MEDICAL OFFICER 

 122  

 Procedure on death of inmate 

 On the death of any inmate, the medical officer must enter on the inmate’s clinical record the following particulars— 

 (a) 

 the time of onset of illness: 

 (b) 

 the time of his or her being advised of the illness: 

 (c) 

 the nature of the illness: 

 (d) 

 the time and date of death: 

 (e) 

 if an autopsy has been performed, an account of the findings: 

 (f) 

 any relevant remarks.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF MEDICAL OFFICER 

 123  

 Inmate unfit for detention 

 (1)  

 Whenever the medical officer has reason to believe that any inmate’s mental or physical health has been or likely to be injuriously affected by continued detention or by any conditions of detention, or that the life of any inmate will be endangered by detention, or that any sick inmate will not survive his or her sentence or is totally or permanently unfit for detention, the medical officer must, without delay, report the case in writing to the Superintendent with such recommendations as he or she thinks fit. 

 (2)  

 The Superintendent must forward such report and recommendations to the Director forthwith.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF MEDICAL OFFICER 

 124  

 Recommendations as to work 

 On medical grounds, the medical officer may recommend that any inmate be excused from work, or that the nature of his or her work be changed.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF MEDICAL OFFICER 

 125  

 Suicidal inmate 

 The medical officer must draw the attention of the Superintendent to any inmate who, in his or her opinion, has suicidal intentions, in order that the inmate may be specially watched, and the Superintendent shall without delay direct that the inmate be observed at frequent intervals.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF MEDICAL OFFICER 

 126  

 Mental health 

 The medical officer must keep under special observation every inmate whose mental condition appears to require it, and shall recommend such steps as he or she considers proper for the inmate’s care.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF MEDICAL OFFICER 

 127  

 Prison officers and candidates 

 (1)  

 The medical officer must from time to time, as required by the Director, examine officers or candidates for admission to the prison service. 

 (2)  

 No charge may be made to any officer or candidate for any examination pursuant to this regulation.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF MEDICAL OFFICER 

 128  

 Inspections 

 At least once in every 3 months, and whenever required by the Director, the medical officer must inspect every part of the prison and must send to the Director, through the Superintendent, a report on the cleanliness of the prison, the drainage, warmth, and ventilation, the quality of the provisions, the adequacy of clothing and bedding, the quantity and quality of the water, and any other matters which may affect the health of the inmates; and must draw attention to any deficiencies.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF MEDICAL OFFICER 

 129  

 Record of visits 

 The medical officer must ensure that at each visit made by him or her a record is maintained in the prison of the times of his or her arrival and departure.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF DENTAL OFFICER 

 130  

 Dental examinations 

 (1)  

 Wherever desirable a dental officer must examine every inmate being detained in the prison for more than 3 months as soon after the inmate’s admission as possible, and must enter the required particulars on a dental history sheet. 

 (2)  

 The dental officer must also enter on the dental history sheet details of any subsequent examinations and treatment.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF DENTAL OFFICER 

 131  

 Duties 

 (1)  

 The dental officer shall be primarily concerned with the relief of pain, the maintenance of a reasonable dental standard, and the repair of dentures. 

 (2)  

 The dental officer obtain the prior approval of the Director before doing either of the following things, namely— 

 (a) 

 full extractions in either jaw or both: 

 (b) 

 the provision of full or partial dentures.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF DENTAL OFFICER 

 132  

 Record of visits 

 The dental officer must ensure that at each visit a record is maintained in the prison of the time of his or her arrival and departure.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF SUPERINTENDENT 

 133  

 Inmate requiring medical attention 

 (1)  

 At each visit of the medical officer to a prison the Superintendent must supply him or her with a list of the names of all inmates who— 

 (a) 

 have not been medically examined since admission; or 

 (b) 

 complain of illness or have requested to see the medical officer; or 

 (c) 

 appear to require medical attention or examination; or 

 (d) 

 have been sentenced to restricted diet; or 

 (e) 

 are confined in punishment cells. 

 (2)  

 The Superintendent must without delay draw the attention of the medical officer to any inmate whose state of body or mind appears to require examination or attention.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF SUPERINTENDENT 

 134  

 Use of mechanical restraint 

 Where mechanical restraint is used in respect of any inmate, except in the case of its use during his or her transfer or removal or on the recommendation of the medical officer on medical grounds, the Superintendent must inform the medical officer without delay.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF SUPERINTENDENT 

 135  

 Contagious or infectious disease 

 (1)  

 The Superintendent must take precautions to prevent the spread of contagious or infectious disease. 

 (2)  

 Every inmate suffering from or suspected to be suffering from any contagious or infectious disease, and such other inmate as may be recommended by the medical officer, must be kept strictly separate from other inmates. 

 (3)  

 All infected clothing and bedding shall on the recommendation of the medical officer be specially treated or destroyed.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 DUTIES OF SUPERINTENDENT 

 136  

 Dealing with recommendations 

 Any written recommendation by the medical officer or a visiting specialist must either— 

 (a) 

 be given effect to by the Superintendent, who must enter on the link sheet or specialist’s recommendation when and how it was given effect to and any remarks he or she wishes to make: 

 (b) 

 in any case here, in the Superintendent’s opinion, the recommendation may affect the discipline or security of the prison, or for any other reason whatever he or she considers it should first be referred to the Director, it must be reported to the Director, who must give whatever instructions he or she thinks proper in the circumstances.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 EXERCISE 

 137  

 Exercise 

 Every inmate must be allowed at least as much fresh air and exercise as the medical officer considers necessary for the preservation of health.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 ACCOMMODATION 

 138  

 Sleeping accommodation 

 (1)  

 Where sleeping accommodations in individual cells, only one inmate may occupy each cell. 

 (2)  

 Where sleeping accommodation is not in individual cells current Health Department regulations as to accommodation standards must be observed. 

 (3)  

 Where there is a shortage of accommodation the Superintendent may, with the approval of the Director (given either generally or in a particular case) and with the concurrence of the medical officer in the particular case; authorise the accommodation of more than one inmate in a cell or, as the case may be, the provision of sleeping accommodation which does not comply with the standards mentioned in subclause (2); 
 Provided that in an emergency it is necessary for the Superintendent to obtain the approval of the Director or the concurrence of the medical officer but they must afterwards be notified as soon as possible.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 BEDDING AND CLOTHING 

 139  

 Bedding and clothing 

 Every inmate may be provided with a separate bed, and with separate bedding and an outfit of clothing adequate for warmth and health in accordance with the general scale prescribed by the Director and in conformity with any direction of the medical officer.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 BEDDING AND CLOTHING 

 140  

 Laundering of bedding, etc 

 Every blanket and bedding cover must be laundered, at least twice in every year.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 FOOD 

 141  

 Diet 

 Every inmate must be supplied with a sufficient quantity of wholesome food which, except as provided in regulation 74, must be not less than that specified in the scale approved from time to time by the Director and the Director of Health: 
 Provided that for any particular inmate the medical officer may from time to time prescribe a different diet, or any variation in the approved diet.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 PERSONAL HYGIENE 

 142  

 Bathing 

 Every inmate must have a bath or a shower at least twice a day.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 PERSONAL HYGIENE 

 143  

 Hair 

 (1)  

 Every male inmate’s hair may be cut on admission, and thereafter must be kept reasonably short. 

 (2)  

 Every male inmate must shave daily or as often as is required for a reasonable appearance. He may be permitted to retain a beard or a moustache which he has on admission, but may not be permitted to grow either while he is in the prison. 

 (3)  

 The Superintendent may, for any reason that he or she thinks sufficient, direct that all or any of the foregoing provisions of this regulation do not apply to any inmate. 

 (4)  

 No female inmate’s hair may be cut without her consent, unless the medical officer directs it on the grounds of health or cleanliness.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 INMATES AWAITING TRIAL OR ON REMAND 

 144  

 Interpretation 

 In this Part inmate awaiting trial means an inmate detained only by reason of the fact that he or she is awaiting trial or is on remand during the trial or before sentence.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 INMATES AWAITING TRIAL OR ON REMAND 

 145  

 Separation from other inmates 

 Inmates awaiting trial must, so far as practicable, be kept apart from inmates.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 INMATES AWAITING TRIAL OR ON REMAND 

 146  

 Retention of property in cell 

 So far as is consistent with discipline and the good order or the prison, the Superintendent may allow any inmate awaiting trial to have in his or her cell any articles that were in his or her possession at the time of his or her admission and are not required for the purposes of justice or reasonably suspected or forming part of property improperly acquired by him.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 INMATES AWAITING TRIAL OR ON REMAND 

 147  

 Inmates committed in same case 

 So far as circumstances will permit, inmates awaiting trial and committed in the same case must be kept separate and must not be permitted to communicate with each other.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 INMATES AWAITING TRIAL OR ON REMAND 

 148  

 Visitors 

 Subject to regulations 107, 108, 109, and 110 and regulation 106(2) and (4), every inmate awaiting trial must be afforded all reasonable facilities for receiving visitors at reasonable times on any day except Christmas Day, Boxing Day, New Year’s Day, Anzac Day, Good Friday, Easter Monday, Queen’s Birthday Constitution Day, Saturday, and Sunday; and may be afforded facilities on any such day if the Superintendent approves.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 INMATES AWAITING TRIAL OR ON REMAND 

 149  

 Interviews with legal adviser 

 Any interview between an inmate awaiting trial and his or her legal advisers may be held in the sight, but not in the hearing, of a prison officer.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 INMATES AWAITING TRIAL OR ON REMAND 

 150  

 Treatment by doctor or dentist 

 Where at the time of his or her admission to the prison any inmate awaiting trial is undergoing urgent medical or dental treatment he or she may, at the discretion of the Superintendent, be visited and treated by his or her own medical practitioner or dentist. Any expense so incurred is the responsibility of the inmate.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 INMATES AWAITING TRIAL OR ON REMAND 

 151  

 Correspondence, etc 

 (1)  

 Subject to regulations 105 and 104(3), (4), and (5), every inmate awaiting trial must be afforded all reasonable facilities for writing to or receiving letters from other persons. 

 (2)  

 A confidential written communication prepared as instructions for the legal adviser of an inmate awaiting trial may be delivered personally to that legal adviser and must not be treated as a letter to which regulation 105(1) applies unless the Superintendent has reason to suppose that it contains matter not relating to those instructions. 

 (3)  

 Paper and all other writing materials, to an extent as appears reason to the Superintendent, must be provided for any inmate awaiting trial who requires it for the purposes of preparing a defence.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 INMATES AWAITING TRIAL OR ON REMAND 

 152  

 Tobacco, food, clothing, etc 

 Every inmate awaiting trial is permitted to procure at his own expense or receive from his or her friends reasonable quantities of tobacco, food, clothing and other necessaries for his or her own use.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 INMATES AWAITING TRIAL OR ON REMAND 

 153  

 Prison clothing 

 (1)  

 Every inmate awaiting trial may wear prison clothing if he or she so desires, and must do so if he or she volunteers to work. 

 (2)  

 An inmate awaiting trial is required to wear prison clothing if his or her own clothes are insufficient or unfit for use or are required to be preserved for the purposes of justice.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 INMATES AWAITING TRIAL OR ON REMAND 

 154  

 Hair 

 Except on the ground of health or cleanliness, the hair, beard, or moustache of any inmate awaiting trial must not be cut except to such extent as may be necessary to preserve his or her appearance as at the time of his or her reception into the prison.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 INMATES AWAITING TRIAL OR ON REMAND 

 155  

 Care of cell and utensils 

 Every inmate awaiting trial is required to keep himself or herself and his or her cell and utensils clean and in good order.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 PERSONS COMMITTED FOR DEFAULT OR CONTEMPT 

 156  

 Separation from other inmates 

 So far as practicable, inmates who are detained only in respect of the non-payment of a sum of money, or only for non-compliance with an order of any court, or only for contempt of court, must be kept apart from other inmates.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 INMATES UNDER 21 

 157  

 Separation from adult inmates 

 So far as practicable, inmates under the age of 21 years, whether they are inmates awaiting trial or inmates detained after conviction, must be kept apart from inmates of or over that age.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 APPELLANTS 

 158  

 Appeal against conviction 

 (1)  

 Subject to the provisions of this regulation, where to the knowledge of the Superintendent any inmate has appealed or applied for leave to appeal against any conviction or order, and that inmate is in custody only under the conviction or order to which the appeal or application relates, the inmate must, pending the determination of his or her appeal or application, be specially treated in the same manner as an inmate awaiting trial. 

 (2)  

 As soon as it comes to the knowledge of the Superintendent that any inmate to whom subclause (1) applies has appealed or applied for leave to appeal he or she must cause the inmate to be informed that he or she may, if he or she wishes, elect not to be specially treated as an inmate awaiting trial. 

 (3)  

 If the inmate so elects, he or she must be treated in the manner required by his or her sentence, and while he or she is so treated the term of his or her detention under his or her sentence continues to run. 

 (4)  

 Any inmate who has so elected as aforesaid may at any time revoke his or her election by informing the Superintendent that he or she wishes to do so; and thereafter he or she must, pending the determination of his or her appeal or application, be specially treated as an inmate awaiting trial, and is not entitled to make any further election. 

 (5)  

 For the purposes of this regulation, an inmate is not deemed to be in custody only under the conviction or order to which the appeal or application relates if any other sentence or term of imprisonment is cumulative on the sentence imposed on that conviction or order and he or she has not appealed or applied for leave to appeal against the conviction or order in respect of which the cumulative sentence or term was imposed.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 APPELLANTS 

 159  

 Appeal against sentence 

 (1)  

 Subject to the provisions of this regulation, every inmate who has appealed, or applied or leave to appeal, only against a sentence imposed on him or her must pending the determination of his or her appeal or application, be treated in the manner required by the sentence. 

 (2)  

 Any inmate who has appealed or applied for leave to appeal against a conviction or order, and is not in custody only under the conviction or order to which the appeal or application relates, must, pending the determination or his or her appeal or application, be treated as if no such appeal or application had been made. 

 (3)  

 For the purposes of his or her appeal or application the inmate may receive visits from a medical practitioner or other professional adviser selected by him, or by his or her friends or his or her legal adviser, under the same conditions as those applying to visits by his or her legal adviser. 

 (4)  

 The provisions or regulation 151(2) and (3) apply to the inmate as if he or she were an inmate awaiting trial and as if the preparation of the appeal or application were the preparation of his or her defence.

PRISONS REGULATIONS 1968 

 APPELLANTS 

 160  

 Removal to High Court or Supreme Court of New Zealand 

 Where any inmate has been granted leave to be present at any proceedings before the High Court or the Supreme Court of New Zealand, or an order has been made that any inmate be taken to any place for the purpose or such proceedings, the inmate must be escorted by an officer and must, unless his or her release is ordered by the court, remain in the custody of the officer while he or she is absent from the prison.
